_comment: SxS Literature Review Quality — Run 2 of 2 (ORDER SWAPPED). paper_1 = human-authored original intro+RW; paper_2 = paper-orc generated intro+RW.
paper_1_analysis: Paper 1's Introduction proceeds in four paragraphs that move from the LLM-personality literature, through the validity-check requirement, to a list of six existing critiques and a four-stage causal-chain summary. Related Work has three subsections — Personality Measurement in LLMs; Response Style and Acquiescence Bias; Alignment Effects on LLM Behavior — each closing with an 'Our contribution' \paragraph that explicitly contrasts the present audit with the cited literature. The voice is more conversational than typical ACL prose ('The cracks are already visible. We do.'). Citation count is 26 unique works in Intro + Related Work — approximately 50% of the assumed ACL/EMNLP baseline of ~52 citations per paper. Foundational methodological anchors (Kaiser, Horn, Tucker, Couch & Keniston, Crowne & Marlowe, Vandenberg & Lance, Meredith) are absent from these sections; Cronbach 1951 and Lord & Novick 1968 are the only methodological foundations cited.
paper_2_analysis: Paper 2's Introduction proceeds in five paragraphs that move from framing, through the missing measurement question, to the empirical design, then a four-stage cascade preview with explicit quantitative milestones (rho = -1.0, Tucker phi = 0.993, inter-model variance < 1%), and finally a persona-stress summary. A 7-bullet contribution list closes the Introduction. Related Work has three structured subsections — LLM personality profiling and silicon samples; response styles, acquiescence, and social desirability; alignment, RLHF, and behavioural side effects — each closing with a bridge-to-our-method synthesis sentence. Citation count is 57 unique works in Intro + Related Work (~110% of the assumed ACL/EMNLP baseline), and the review includes foundational psychometric anchors (Cronbach 1951; Couch & Keniston 1960; Crowne & Marlowe 1960; Kaiser 1958, 1960; Horn 1965; Tucker 1951; Meredith 1993; Vandenberg & Lance 2000) plus recent precedents (Suhr 2025; Pelet 2025; Han 2025; Sharma 2024; Acerbi 2024; Salecha 2024).
comparison_justification: On Problem Framing and Motivation, both papers state the gap; Paper 2's silicon-sample framing is more concrete about downstream impact. On Coverage of Prior Work, Paper 2 cites 57 unique works (vs Paper 1's 26) and includes the foundational methodological anchors that Paper 1 omits. The omission matters because the paper's central thesis is that the LLM-personality literature has skipped the standard human-subjects validation toolkit — citing that toolkit explicitly is a load-bearing element. On Organization and Synthesis, both papers use three parallel Related-Work subsections; Paper 2's overview → SOTA → limitation → bridge pattern is slightly more explicit than Paper 1's 'Our contribution' paragraph format. On Positioning of the Contribution, Paper 2's 7-bullet itemised list with bold tags is sharper than Paper 1's prose-only positioning. On Writing Quality, both are clean; Paper 2 is slightly tighter, and Paper 1 has slightly more conversational language that may or may not appeal to ACL reviewers. The decisive criterion is Coverage of Prior Work: Paper 2's citation breadth, including foundational methodological anchors that match the paper's argumentative spine, is materially stronger.
